claims.statement: The documented birth record concerns Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo's birth is dated 15 April 1452.
The documented birthplace is Vinci at named-settlement precision.
This birth anchor establishes the evidenced beginning of the bounded whole-life trajectory.
The 1472 Compagnia di San Luca entry concerns Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo's registration with the painters' confraternity is dated to 1472 at year precision.
The documented confraternity context places this anchor in Florence at named-city precision.
This anchor represents Leonardo's documented Florentine artistic formation in the bounded trajectory.
The surviving 1483 altarpiece contract names Leonardo as a commissioned painter.
The surviving contract is dated 25 April 1483; the candidate Presence is normalized only to the year 1483.
The contract documents a Milan commission context at named-city precision, not Leonardo's exact body position.
This contract anchor provides the bounded package's documentary marker for Leonardo's first Milan phase.
The artist described as back in Florence in 1503 is Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo's return is anchored to 1503 at year precision.
The documented return places this anchor in Florence at named-city precision.
This anchor restores the major Florence phase while preserving the finer frozen Romagna 1502 segment.
The Manuscript F incipit is Leonardo da Vinci's dated notebook record.
The Manuscript F incipit is dated 12 September 1508.
The incipit explicitly names Milan, supporting named-city precision only.
This source-native day anchor provides the bounded package's documentary marker for Leonardo's second Milan phase.
The Roman and Belvedere chronology entries concern Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo's Roman phase is bounded to 1513–1516 at year-range precision.
The documented residence/work context is Rome and the Vatican Belvedere complex, without exact room geometry.
This bounded residence/work anchor represents Leonardo's major Roman phase in the whole-life trajectory.
The final Clos Lucé residence described by the source concerns Leonardo da Vinci.
Leonardo settled at Clos Lucé during autumn 1516 and died there on 2 May 1519; the possible start is bounded to September–November 1516.
The documented final residence is Clos Lucé in Amboise at named-residence precision.
This residence/death anchor establishes the evidenced endpoint of the bounded whole-life trajectory.
